headline: Record revenue and backlog fuel a second guidance raise
summary_short: Motorola Solutions' Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 13.3% y/y to $3,133M with diluted GAAP EPS of $3.33 (+9.5% y/y), driven by record backlog ($15.6B, +11% y/y) and margin expansion; the company again raised full-year revenue and non-GAAP EPS guidance.
summary_long: Revenue rose 15.4% q/q and 13.3% y/y to $3,133M, led by 15% growth in Products & Systems Integration and 10% in Software & Services, plus $243M from acquisitions and a $35M FX tailwind. GAAP operating margin expanded to 25.8% (+80bp y/y) and non-GAAP margin to 32.9% (+330bp y/y), aided by a $60M IEEPA tariff-refund benefit. Diluted EPS was $3.33 (+9.5% y/y); non-GAAP EPS $4.41 (+24% y/y). Cash fell to $710M (from $3,206M a year ago, when a $1,983M debt issuance inflated the balance); the company still returned $326M via buybacks and $201M in dividends, and agreed to acquire D-Fend Solutions for $1.5B. Full-year revenue and EPS guidance raised again.

Net income growth of 8.6% y/y trailed operating income's 16.7% growth due to higher net interest expense ($103M vs $55M a year ago, on additional debt), partly offset by other income.
